reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents the Forsage marketing plan as member-oriented business guidance with recruitment-linked returns of 200%, 580%, and 1200%, plus bonuses moving to a wallet and a claimed five-minute cashout. The slides show BUSD and TRX/USD amounts within hierarchical member structures. The records do not establish that any transfer, sale, payout, or stated percentage was actually achieved.

citations.quote: 5 Minutes to Understand the Forsage Marketing Plan
if you sponsor 2 people then in the matrix you will be like this
you can get the profit 30% on the second level when you sponsor another 2 members

opening.argument: The material supports a cautious, explanatory reading rather than a promise of personal gain. Its stated purpose is to help members understand a plan and run the business properly, not to document a completed payout. The slides and narration describe how the system is supposed to operate, but the supplied record does not establish that any viewer deposited money, recruited anyone, received a return, or was guaranteed an outcome. Even the displayed examples include an account showing zero BUSD, which is consistent with an illustrative walkthrough rather than proof of earnings.

citations.quote: 5 Minutes to Understand the Forsage Marketing Plan
Understanding the marketing plan is an obligation for every member to be able to run the business on the right track, just 5 minutes...

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats every described percentage as a realized return, but the quoted language explains what the matrix is said to do under particular member arrangements. It does not show that the presenter obtained those amounts or that viewers were promised them. The cited slide is a diagrammatic example, and the record does not establish a completed transaction, solicitation of a specific viewer, or a guaranteed result.

citations.quote: You will get 200% bonus

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the video an explanation does not neutralize its substance. The explanation repeatedly links sponsorship and additional members to stated profits, including “30%” on a second level. A zero-balance illustration does not make the surrounding recruitment-linked claims merely hypothetical or add any risk warning; it only shows one displayed state.

citations.quote: you can get the profit 30% on the second level when you sponsor another 2 members
in total, you add 1200% on the X-gold

opening.argument: The format is most naturally understood as an operational tutorial. The title explicitly says it is a five-minute explanation of the marketing plan, while the narration walks through X3, X4, and XGold levels and describes how slots, levels, reinvestment, and wallet transfers are represented. The screenshots function as demonstrations of interface states and matrix arrangements. Explaining a system, including its claimed economics, is not by itself proof that the speaker is certifying those claims or soliciting a transaction.

citations.quote: 5 Minutes to Understand the Forsage Marketing Plan
How to work X3 X3 has 1 level
after reinvest then your matrix will be empty again like this

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening relies on the existence of diagrams and cryptocurrency labels, but those are exactly what an operational demonstration would be expected to display. A screen showing BUSD and a tree does not establish that the presenter is selling access, collecting funds, or representing the example as a completed personal result. The narration's instructional sequencing also matters: it explains levels, member placement, and reinvestment rather than reporting a verified event.

citations.quote: This is MatrixX4

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial framing does not change what the tutorial teaches. Its instructions center on sponsoring people, filling levels, and receiving percentages from later levels. The claimed profits are not incidental interface mechanics: the narration tells viewers what they can obtain from recruiting members. The screenshots reinforce that the demonstrated structure is a multi-level member tree, not a neutral software tutorial.

at level 3, u get 50%

opening.argument: The record shows a proposed digital-asset cash-flow and account process, not the core evidence needed to infer a scam mechanism. The narration describes bonuses going to a wallet and assets being transferable or saleable, and one slide identifies Trust Wallet and Binance in a rupiah-cashout context. But no supplied frame or text shows a deposit request, credential collection, completed sale, actual payout, or transfer from a viewer. The displayed examples cannot establish that money changed hands, so the strongest grounded conclusion is an explanation of an external service's operating model, not proof of deceptive conduct.

citations.quote: the bonus will be directly transferred to the wallet without a withdrawal
from crypto and indodax stores you can immediately sell your digital assets

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies recruitment language, but recruitment alone does not prove that a deceptive payment mechanism operated in this video. Its own description concedes that the records do not establish a transfer, sale, payout, or achieved percentage. The wallet and exchange references identify tools in the described cash-out route; they do not show the creator taking funds or fabricating a transaction.

citations.quote: we only need to transfer to crypto or indodax stores

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing proof of a completed payout is not exculpatory when the content promotes a recruitment-based earning structure. The narration expressly conditions percentages on sponsoring members and describes a cycle in which the matrix is filled and reinvested. That is the mechanism at issue; a screenshot with zero assets cannot erase the stated downline conditions or convert them into ordinary retail commerce.
